condition: I'm looking for products that serve similar purposes, regardless of their brand or category.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Product.description can provide direct information about a product’s purpose, supporting similarity comparisons without relying on brand or category.
A product title can describe what the product is for, supporting purpose-based similarity without relying on brand or category.
Review text may mention a product’s use or purpose, but it is indirect and the schema does not guarantee that reviews describe this.
Review summaries may mention a product’s use or purpose, but they are review text rather than direct product-purpose attributes, so the evidence is weak and indirect.
Product category may weakly suggest purpose, but the condition explicitly seeks similarity regardless of category, so this signal should not constrain matches.
Product price may weakly reflect a product’s market segment, but it does not directly indicate its purpose.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about products’ purposes or similarity.
Brand is explicitly irrelevant to the condition, and the schema does not indicate that it captures product purpose.
A review rating provides no schema-grounded evidence about product purpose or similarity.
Review time gives no schema-grounded evidence about a product’s purpose or similarity.
review.verified indicates whether a review is verified, but does not describe product purpose or similarity.

condition: Which products appeal to similar customers based on their reviewing behavior?

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text can express customer opinions and preferences, providing behavioral evidence, but this signal alone does not connect reviews to customers or products.
Review ratings directly reflect customers’ evaluations, which can inform product appeal, but this signal alone does not identify which customers reviewed which products or establish similarity.
Review timestamps can provide a temporal aspect of customers’ reviewing behavior, but this signal alone does not link reviews to customers or products.
Customer names can identify customers, but the signal contains no review behavior or product association.
Brand can weakly group products, but it provides no direct evidence about which customers reviewed them or whether their reviewing behavior is similar.
Product category can group products by type, but it does not capture which customers reviewed them or whether their reviewing behavior is similar.
Product descriptions may indicate product similarity, but they do not capture which customers reviewed the products or their reviewing behavior.
Product price may weakly indicate product similarity, but it does not capture which customers review products or their reviewing behavior.
Product title can identify which products are being compared, but it provides no evidence about the customers who review them or their reviewing behavior.
Review summaries may indicate topics or preferences expressed in reviews, but this signal has no customer or product relationship path to connect that behavior to particular customers or products.
The verified flag provides a limited review-level behavior signal, but it does not identify customers, products, or similarity between them.

condition: Show me reviews that provide useful insights into a product's strengths and weaknesses.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review text is a direct source of written feedback that may describe a product’s strengths and weaknesses.
A review’s summary is directly associated with the review and can provide concise evidence about product strengths and weaknesses; its actual content is not specified.
A review rating can indicate overall positive or negative sentiment, helping identify reviews relevant to strengths or weaknesses, but it does not specify what those are.
Product category provides context about the kind of product, but does not indicate whether its reviews describe strengths or weaknesses.
A product description can provide context for interpreting a review’s comments about strengths and weaknesses, but it does not directly indicate whether a review contains useful insights.
Product price may provide context for reviews discussing value, but it does not directly indicate whether a review describes strengths or weaknesses.
A review’s verified status may weakly indicate credibility, but it does not directly show whether the review discusses product strengths or weaknesses.
Brand identifies the product's maker, but does not indicate whether its reviews discuss strengths or weaknesses.
A product title can identify the product being reviewed, but it does not indicate whether review content discusses strengths or weaknesses.
Review time may weakly indicate recency, but it does not show whether the review discusses a product’s strengths or weaknesses.
Customer names provide no schema-grounded evidence about whether a review describes a product’s strengths or weaknesses.

condition: Prioritize products that offer a good balance of price, quality, and customer satisfaction.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review ratings directly indicate customer satisfaction and may provide an imperfect quality signal, but they do not capture product price.
Product price directly informs the price side of the requested balance, but alone provides no evidence about quality or customer satisfaction.
Review text can provide evidence about perceived product quality and customer satisfaction, but this signal contains no price information to assess the balance.
Review summaries can provide qualitative evidence of customer satisfaction and perceived quality, but they do not directly encode product price or establish a product-level balance.
Brand is a product attribute that may help distinguish products, but it does not directly indicate price, quality, or customer satisfaction.
Product category can provide context for comparing products within a category, but it does not directly indicate price, quality, or customer satisfaction.
Product description may provide indirect evidence about quality or features, but it does not directly indicate price or customer satisfaction.
Review time can provide temporal context for customer feedback, but it does not directly indicate product price, quality, or satisfaction.
A review’s verified status may modestly indicate the credibility of customer feedback, but it does not directly measure satisfaction, product quality, or price.
Product titles identify products but do not directly indicate price, quality, or customer satisfaction.
Customer names do not provide schema evidence about product price, quality, or customer satisfaction.

condition: I'd like to discover customers with similar tastes based on their ratings and opinions.

llm_config.evaluation_note: Discovery does not use human or LLM relevance labels.

signals.evidence: Review ratings directly indicate customers’ expressed evaluations and can support comparing tastes across reviews, though this signal alone omits written opinions and customer associations.
Review text directly captures customers’ expressed opinions, but this review-only signal does not connect reviews to customers or include ratings.
Review summaries can capture opinions relevant to taste similarity, but this signal alone does not include ratings or a path to identify customers.
Product brand can indicate a shared preference dimension, but this signal alone does not connect products to customers or include their ratings and opinions.
Product category can weakly indicate the kinds of items relevant to customer tastes, but this signal has no path to reviews or customers and does not capture ratings or opinions.
Product descriptions can provide indirect semantic evidence about the items customers may like, but this signal alone does not capture customer ratings, opinions, or the customer-review associations.
Product price may weakly reflect a price-related preference, but it does not capture ratings or opinions and the stated path does not connect the signal to customers.
Product titles can identify items whose reviews might indicate shared tastes, but the signal alone provides no customer associations, ratings, or opinions.
Review verification may weakly indicate the reliability of an opinion, but it does not capture ratings or opinion content needed to identify similar tastes.
Review time may weakly indicate when customers reviewed products, but it does not directly capture the ratings or opinions that define similar tastes.
Customer name does not indicate ratings or opinions, and the signal path reaches no review data.
